title: Re-architect weight indexing and detached tokenizer init
creator: Maya Patel
description: Background: Our current model ingestion path couples weight activation, shard negotiation, and tokenizer initialization into a single synchronous startup flow. This causes high memory spikes, long cold-start latency for large models, and brittle behavior when weight manifests differ slightly between formats. Goal: Re-architect the ingestion pipeline to (1) introduce a lightweight, versioned weight-index/manifest reader that can stream shard metadata and allow incremental activation, and (2) detach tokenizer initialization so tokenizers can be validated and warmed independently of weight activation. Outcomes: reduced peak memory usage during model open, lower cold-start tail latency, clearer upgrade path for new checkpoint formats, and safer tokenizer upgrades with explicit compatibility checks.
acceptance_criteria: New weight-index format reader can load metadata for 100GB checkpoints in under 3s without allocating weight tensors
Tokenizer init is an independent step that can be executed and validated before any weight tensors are mapped
Backward compatibility shim can load legacy manifests and expose the same index API
Integration tests pass for streaming activation, including simulated networked sharding and partial failures
Measured improvement: >=25% reduction in median model-open latency for 13B+ models and >=30% reduction in peak RSS during open on CI infra
steps: Design and spec versioned weight-index schema (manifest fields, shard ranges, checksums)
Implement lightweight probing reader that fetches and validates shard headers without deserializing tensors
Add activation controller that accepts streaming shard payloads and applies atomic activation semantics
Decouple tokenizer init: new tokenizer contract + compatibility validator and warm cache API
Add backward-compat shim for legacy checkpoint formats to expose the new index API
Create CI harness with synthetic large checkpoints and failure injection
Rollout behind feature flag: local canary -> internal staging -> gradual runtime rollout
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incompatible legacy checkpoints fail under new index contract. Mitigation: compatibility shim and exhaustive ingest tests against historical checkpoints in S3.
Risk: Tokenizer detachment might expose subtle ordering bugs for token-dependent kernels. Mitigation: add end-to-end evals comparing model outputs pre/post-change on canonical prompt suites.
Risk: Activation controller regressions could increase tail latency. Mitigation: perf benchmarks and autoscaling guardrails in Dedicated for rollout.
Risk: Migration complexity across Dedicated and Private deployments. Mitigation: provide migration tool that performs dry-run validation and a rollback path.
testing_plan: Unit tests for weight-index parser and header validators
Fault-injection integration tests: interrupted shard stream, corrupted header, late shard arrival
Performance regression suite: model-open latency, peak memory on representative 7B/13B/70B checkpoints
Tokenizer compatibility matrix tests (BPE/Unigram/custom merges) against canonical tokenizers repo
E2E correctness checks comparing outputs on 200 prompt seeds before and after change
